findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

A CFPM certificate could not be produced for staff at the facility during the inspection. The PIC stated that they were in the process of taking the course and should be receiving the certification in the next little while. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts where foods are being handled/prepared.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The facility was unable to provide a verification that employee were notified of their responsibility to report symptoms/diagnosis related to foodborne illnesses during the inspection. A fresh copy of the Sangamon County Employee Illness Reporting Agreement was given and they were instructed to make copies and have all food handlers sign prior tot he follow up.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The hand sinks next to the three part sink and by the food preparation area were observed blocked at the start of the inspection. The items were removed by the inspector to allow for hand washing to correct. The PIC was notified of the situation and instructed to ensure that all hand sinks are accessible at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The hand sink in one of the bathrooms did not have a functioning method for hand drying. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the they stated that the drying unit was out of service and a work order had already been put in. While that it taking place another method should have been supplied for hand drying until the new installation had taken place. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

Multiple single service containers were observed stored with the food contact surfaces up/exposed in the preparation area. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The items were flipped over during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected from contamination until used.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop was observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink with the mop bucket inverted over it. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the mop moved so that that the bristles hang to correct. Ensure that the mop is stored so that it effectively drys moving forward to prevent possible pest or mold issues in the future.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

The floor under the soda syrups was observed heavily soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink was observed blocked by a towel container in front and a spray bottle inside of it at the start of the inspection. The items were removed by the inspector to allow for hand washing to correct. The PIC was notified of the situation and instructed to ensure that all hand sinks are accessible at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The hand sinks in the food preparation area as well as next to the three part sink are without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced the towels to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The spout of the ice chute on the fountain drink machine is observed with pink growth around the lip where ice comes out. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean regularly along with the fountain drink machine nozzles. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

During this inspection it was noticed that the hand sink next to the 3 part sink is blocked by a wet floor sign and is not easily accessible. The sign was removed to correct.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

PIC was unable to show in a verifiable manner that employee have been notified of their reporting responsibilities. Blank reporting agreements were handed out during this inspection and inspector will follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

1) Two cans and a knife are observed in the hand sink in the food prep area on inspector arrival. 2) (REPEAT) The hand sink next to the three part sink was blocked by with personal items and cleaning items on arrival. Items were moved during the inspection to correct the violations.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival, the hand sink next to the three part sink is observed to not dispense paper towels. The PIC was left with the equipment while the inspector moved on with the inspection and later indicated that the machine had run out. New paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements. 

A bottle of Lysol Kitchen Pro is observed in the food prep area of the facility. The PIC indicated that this is what is used for sanitizing the surfaces in the kitchen. Reading through the label indicates that it is intended for kitchens, but not direct food contact surfaces. Testing of the solution indicates a toxic level of Quat as the active chemical. Education was conducted with the PIC and the item removed. The PIC indicated that it would be used on the counters out on the floor but no longer in the food prep area. The Quat solution used in the three part sink will be used moving foreword.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

The right fountain drink machine is heavily soiled around the drain spouts and back edges of the catch tray. Clean this area and ensure that it is maintained cleaned moving foreword.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

A cleaning bucket under the three part sink is observed filled with water and other cleaning supplies. There is significant growth throughout the water indicating a long period of inactivity. The bucket and items were discarded during this inspection to correct. Ensure that this situation does not present again in the future.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

The mop is observed stored in soiled mop water in the mop bucket. Storage was discussed and it is suggested to let it hang over the ringer to dry. Ensure that the mop is stored so that it can hang/dry moving foreword.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations through out the facility need to be swept and (where possible) mopped. Locations noted include, but are not limited to, the gaps around the standing cooler in the prep area (possible dried mouse droppings), behind stacks of drinks in the prep room and under shelves and sinks in the manager’s room. Clean all areas of the facility consistently enough to prevent filth accumulation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

PIC during the inspection was unable to provide verification of employee food handler training. PIC should maintain copies so that they are available for inspector observation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of this inspection, no certified food protection manager is available at the facility. Multiple food items are observed on the hot dog rollers and popcorn is in the machine. Due to bing a Class-II facility, a CFPM must be on site at all times that food handling/preparation  activities are being conducted. Ensure enough CFPM’s are available to cover all shifts where RTE (Ready-To-Eat) foods are being served/handled.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

PIC was unable to show in a verifiable manner that employee have been notified of their reporting responsibilities. Reporting agreements were handed out during this inspection and inspector will follow up on 4/6/23.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink is observed without warn water. PIC indicated that the hot water line was turned off due to a leak. He is instructed to repair the sink prior to the follow up in two weeks.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink was blocked by a trash can, long handled dust pan, coffee maker and plastic soda tray on arrival. Items were moved during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. 

Four of the five hand sinks in the facility are without proper signage during this inspection. Hand washing signs were given to PIC during this inspection and they are instructed to place them up to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper disposition of returned, previously served, reconditioned and unsafe food
findings.comment:
3-701.11: (A) FOOD unsafe, ADULTERATED, or not honestly presented shall be discarded or reconditioned. (B) FOOD not from APPROVED source shall be discarded. (C) RTE FOOD that may have been contaminated from RESTRICTED/EXCLUDED employee shall be discarded. (D) FOOD contaminated by hands, bodily discharges, or other means shall be discarded. 

16 oz bottles of chocolate milk in the display/ walk-in cooler are observed with use by dates of 3/21/23 (two days ago). These items should have been discarded at that time at the latest. PIC was consulted and the items discarded during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

1) A spray bottle next to the hand sink next to the coffee machines has a label of sanitizer, but in actuality contains a general cleaner. 2) A spray bottle with a blue solution in it does not have a label and is identified as window cleaner. 3) A spray bottle with a mostly clear solution in the cooking area does not have a label. It was identified as degreaser. PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that all chemicals have accurate labeling at all times. The containers were relabeled during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

A moist wiping cloth is observed on the counter in the back of th facility. Cloth was moved during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

PIC during the inspection was unable to provide verification of employee food handler training during this inspection. PIC should maintain copies so that they are available for inspector observation.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Manager was not present during the inspection. Food was actively cooking on the roller grills. Food was removed and food preparation ceased immediately. Ensure that a certified food manager is present during all food-preparation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The sanitizer bottle next to the microwave at the front of the facility was observed to have a concentration which exceeded the testing parameters of the test strips (bleaching). Sanitizer was dumped; corrected on site. Operator was unaware of where test strips are in the facility. Ensure that sanitizer is maintained at proper food-contact concentrations and that operators are aware of testing procedures and criteria. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The person-in-charge has not been able to demonstrate knowledge throughout the operation. PIC is does not have a current, valid CFM certificate. The facility has had several priority and priority foundation violations. Active managerial control appears lacking as employees seem to be unaware of proper practices and are not being educated properly on food handling requirements to prevent future violations of the 2017 FDA Food Code. As such, a follow-up is issued for 30-days to evaluate the condition of the facility and the person-in-charge at that time. Inspector will return on 1/09/2023. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Facility had no manager present upon arrival. Manager was contacted to come to facility due to severity of violations observed. Manager is not a current certified food manager (CFM). CFM certificate expired on February 18, 2022. Ensure that person-in-charge has a valid CFM certificate by the next routine inspection. Operator was provided with information regarding CFM certification courses and stated that both himself and new assistant manager have valid CFM certificates. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
During the inspection, facility only had one operating hand washing sink available to employees in the back storage/food preparation area. No hand washing sink is available in the kitchen due to the hand washing sink being inoperable during the inspection per manager. Manager states that the sink at the front of the house near the coffee machines is not used for hand washing and is not stocked as such. Due to the size of the facility and to facilitate frequent and effective hand washing practices, the sink in the office/cleaning area must be repaired and made available. Ensure that the hand sink is repaired and accessible to all employees. 

5-203.11: (A) Specified under LAW, facility must have a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEESS. (B) If APPROVED, automatic handwashing may be substituted. (C) IF APPROVED, chemically treated towelettes can be used.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the open and in-use containers of soda hooked to the soda machine were used for storage of wiping cloths, first-aid materials, signage, and other items which were stored on top of the containers. Open soda containers are not to be used as shelving for storage. Ensure that food is protected from contamination. This is a repeat violation from inspection dated 12/13/2021. A follow-up is issued for 12/12/2022 due to the weekend.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No sanitizer was available throughout the course of the inspection. Bottles of sanitizer were empty/not working and only a small portion of fluid remained at the bottom. Upon testing the “sanitizer” remaining at the bottom of these spray bottles (2 labeled sanitizer, 2 labeled bleach water) none of the containers registered on the inspectors test strips except for one. The one which did register was not diluted and thus bleached out the test strip but the bottle was not functioning and the level of the liquid in the bottle was below the level of the spray hose so no liquid could be sprayed. The facility must have sanitizer available at all times. Ensure that sanitizer bottles are filled and buckets are available as needed are are measuring to the appropriate concentration. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper disposition of returned, previously served, reconditioned and unsafe food
findings.comment:
Soiled and decomposing food was observed to be offered for sale in the facility including visibly discolored salami significantly past date marking times and individually packaged containers of caramel and apples in which the container had been bulging and producing condensation within the package for a significant amount of time and the apples had become rotten to the point of being nearly unrecognizable as apples. Eggs and milk were also offered for sale past the expiration date on the carton (November 18 eggs, December 6 milk). These foods were immediately discarded by person-in-charge. Corrected on site. Ensure that unsafe foods are discarded immediately. 

3-701.11: (A) FOOD unsafe, ADULTERATED, or not honestly presented shall be discarded or reconditioned. (B) FOOD not from APPROVED source shall be discarded. (C) RTE FOOD that may have been contaminated from RESTRICTED/EXCLUDED employee shall be discarded. (D) FOOD contaminated by hands, bodily discharges, or other means shall be discarded.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several opened/working containers of foods in the “True” upright coolers at the rear of the facility with date marking with the facility use-by-date significantly past (as far back as August 2022). Foods included but was not limited to gravy, chicken, ranch dressing, tuna salad, and others. All items with date marking past the date on the date marking or without date marking were voluntarily discarded by person-in-charge immediately. Corrected on site. Ensure that foods which are opened or in working containers bear a proper date marking label and that foods retained past 7 days are discarded.

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed first aid items in an unsealed, perforated plastic container sitting on top of open soda containers in the facility. First aid items must be stored in a kit or container which prevents contamination of food surfaces. Move the first aid items to a location away from food and ensure that these items are stored properly. 

7-208.11: (A) First aid supplies that are in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for EMPLOYEES’ shall be labeled properly (Pf). (B) Shall be stored in kit or container preventing contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (P).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed in-use insecticide spray without a lid and the spray nozzle exposed sitting on top of opened soda containers in the area with the triple sink hooked to the machines out front. Insecticides must be stored away from food, never on top of it, and in a manner which prevents contamination. Inspector also observed a container of gasoline stored next to open and closed soda containers in the office/kitchen with the triple sink. Hazardous substances must be stored away from food. Ensure that these containers of poisonous chemicals are removed from food preparation/service areas and stored in a manner which prevents contamination. A follow-up is being issued for 12/12/2022. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be several soiled wiping cloths sitting out on sinks, counters and other equipment throughout the facility. Wiping cloths must either be laundered or stored in sanitizer solution when not in use. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored and laundered properly. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed brush sitting on top of soiled cardboard on top of a shelf in the sandwich prep area. Utensil is not being cleaned with proper frequency as the utensil was left from food preparation activities which had ceased earlier in the day. Ensure that utensils used for food preparation are cleaned when no longer in use. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Clean tongs were stored in a container above the triple sink with the handle of the tongs along the upper edge of the container and the food contact ends touching the bottom of the container and the visibly soiled shelf the container was sitting on. Clean utensils must be stored in a manner which prevents contamination by ensuring that food contact surfaces of the utensils are not in contact with surfaces that are not cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that clean utensils are stored properly. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following areas that need to be repaired/replaced/re-caulked to ensure that surfaces are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable:
- Caulking behind the triple sink has deteriorated and needs to be replaced
- There is a hole in the ceiling tile above the clean dish portion of the triple sink which needs to be repaired 
- There is a missing ceiling tile above food storage which must be replaced
Ensure that these areas are fixed and that surfaces are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be half drank containers of water stored in the walk in cooler immediately above food intended for purchase. Personal drinks must be stored in a location away from food that prevents contamination. Ensure that there is a designated area for employee drinks which is away from food and that employees are instructed to use the designated area ONLY. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Handsink near the 3 compartment sink observed without paper towels. CORRECTED— PIC provided paper towels.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Handsink near the 3 compartment sink observed to be blocked by a trash can and a bucket in the basin. CORRECTED— PIC moved items so that handsink is accessible.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No signage present indicating that the sink near the 3 compartment sink is only for handwashing. CORRECTED— Inspector provided “Employees Must Wash Hands” signage to be posted.
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: No soap present at the handwashing sink near the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED— PIC provided soap.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Three shell eggs observed stored on the top shelf of the 3 door cooler in the food prep area, above tomatoes, peppers, cheese, and other ready-to-eat foods. CORRECTED— PIC rearranged storage to prevent possible cross contamination. Store raw foods (including eggs) below those that are ready-to-eat.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Dried milk residue observed in the walk-in cooler below where the milk is displayed. Clean as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Hand washing sink in the office/3 compartment sink area was blocked by boxes and a hamper. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. CORRECTED- PIC moved items so that the handwashing sink is easily accessible.
5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

Liquid hand soap not provided at the hand washing sink. Soap dispenser is broken. Provide liquid soap at hand washing sink. CORRECTED- PIC provided soap jug until dispenser can be repaired or replaced.
6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. (Pf)

A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. Provide a clearly visible handwashing sign at each hand sink. CORRECTED- Inspector provided EMPLOYEES MUST WASH HANDS signage.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. (C)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Use by date of 12/10 marked on salami; 12/12 on shredded cheese; 12/12 marked on chocolate pudding exceeds the time limit. Ensure foods are not held past their use-by date. CORRECTED- Employee stated that foods marked "use by 12/12" would be discarded today (12/13). Also stated that salami had been incorrectly labeled 12/10. Foods were discarded, salami was relabeled with correct date-marking.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. (Pf)

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment: Observed a bucket nearly full of brown wastewater under the coffee counter sink. All sewage discharge must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. CORRECTED- PIC emptied bucket. Monitor and repair plumbing as needed. (No active leak was observed during this inspection.)
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. (P)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed boxes, open bottles, and debris found throughout the facility. Clean floors. 
6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (C)

Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use (a wet mop stored upright in the mop sink).
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. (C)
